title: Private CP deployment orchestration checklist & commissioning notes
content:
Purpose
---
This doc is a pragmatic, operational runbook for commissioning and operating a Private Control Plane (Private-CP) in customer VPC / on-prem environments. It focuses on the orchestration steps we follow, Terraform module gotchas, upgrade sequencing, node rotation patterns, and quick rollback options. Intended audience: field SREs, solutions eng, and platform engineers doing initial installs or scale/rotation work.

Scope & non-goals
- Scope: initial commissioning, scale-up/down, instance/node rotations, and minor patch upgrades to control-plane components (operator, api-server, auth proxies, kms connectors).
- Non-goals: full application install (customer data plane), air-gap packaging procedures (see airgapped-cp-setup doc), or platform billing/contract changes.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
1) Validate network & DNS: ensure VPC peering, subnets, route tables, and firewall rules allow control-plane traffic between management hosts and nodes.
2) Remote state + locking: always enable S3/GCS backend with Dynamo/Cloud KMS locks. No local state.
3) Canary nodes: bring up a 1-node canary control-plane; run smoke tests; only then scale to full cluster.
4) Rotation: drain, replace or reprovision; avoid simultaneous rotations of >20% control-plane capacity.
5) Rollback: keep last-known-good TF state snapshot and a small inventory of AMIs/container images for immediate fallback.

Prereqs checklist (before you start)
- Tickets: JIRA ticket exists and is linked to change calendar.
- Credentials: operator keys, KMS access, customer VPC admin, and Terraform service principal with least-privilege that can create network, compute, and storage.
- Backups: control-plane etcd snapshots are configured and recent snapshot stored off-cluster.
- Monitoring: prometheus/metric-exporter endpoint reachable and alerts configured for control-plane-SLOs.
- Inventory: AMI/container image IDs and image provenance recorded in CHANGELOG.
- Approvals: security signoff for required port openings (see firewall section).

Network & DNS validations (commands to run)
- Confirm connectivity from management host to control-plane node:
  - curl -vk https://<control-plane-ip>:8443/healthz
  - nc -vz <node-ip> 2380 (etcd peer)
- DNS: confirm control-plane hostnames resolve to internal VIP (or load-balancer IP):
  - dig @10.0.0.2 controlplane.company.internal +short
- Firewall rules: ensure ephemeral ports for grpc are allowed between nodes (TCP 7000-7100 as configured).

Terraform module notes and common gotchas
- Backend: always use remote backend with state locking (S3 + DynamoDB or GCS + etcd).
- Provider credentials: avoid long-lived cred in TF file; use workspace credentials.
- Module inputs we commonly forget:
  - controlplane_instance_type (defaults may under-provision - prefer m5.large equivalent for 1st pass)
  - enable_kms_rotation (boolean) - if true, ensure KMS key policy includes "terraform-sa"
  - bootstrap_admin_public_key - must be present for emergency SSH into init node
- Resource ordering: terraform plan may reorder LB -> instances causing transient 502s. Use explicit depends_on in module to prevent LB replacement before nodes healthy.
- Upgrade path: when bumping module version, run plan and inspect changes to certs, secrets, and etcd resource replacement counts.
- State drift: we frequently see drift in security group rules managed elsewhere; add guardrails: terraform import and update state before apply.
- Recreate risks: changing subnet ids or AZ lists will trigger instance recreation. Schedule maintenance window.

Commissioning sequence (canonical)
1) Kickoff & change window open
   - Confirm maintenance calendar and pager rotations.
2) Preflight validations (15–30m)
   - Run network & DNS validations above.
   - Confirm IAM/service accounts have necessary roles.
3) Initialize TF workspace (10m)
   - terraform init -backend-config=...
   - terraform workspace select <env> || terraform workspace new <env>
4) Plan & peer review (15–20m)
   - terraform plan -out=tfplan.binary
   - Export plan summary and attach to ticket for reviewer.
5) Apply canary (30–45m)
   - terraform apply -auto-approve tfplan.binary on a constrained size (1 control-plane node + LB)
   - Post-apply checks: health endpoints, logs, certificates present, etcd initial member list.
6) Smoke tests (15–30m)
   - curl /healthz, run k8s API lint tests, run a small create/delete resource test (namespace + pod).
7) Scale to baseline (45–90m)
   - Update TF variables to desired capacity and apply. Monitor metrics for CPU, latency, etc.
8) Final validation & handoff (30m)
   - Create final ticket comment with links to logs, dashboards, and test results.

Minor upgrade plan (patch-level control-plane components)
- Target: rolling restarts without loss of quorum.
- Rough sequence:
  1) Bump module image tag or Terraform var.
  2) Apply a single-node restart for canary; wait 10m and validate metrics.
  3) If canary OK, use controlled rolling update: drain -> upgrade -> uncordon for each node.
  4) Wait for etcd leader election stability between nodes (monitor leader changes).
- Risk mitigations: keep two healthy nodes during upgrades if cluster size <=3; for 3-node clusters keep at least 2 available.

Node rotation patterns (preferred)
- Replace pattern (recommended for config drift): provision new node, add to cluster, migrate workloads, then drain+terminate old node. Avoid in-place reprovision when configuration drift root cause is unknown.
- In-place restart (use only for minor binary patch): systemctl restart controlplane.service -> verify health.
- Stagger windows: rotate 1 node at a time for clusters <=5 nodes; for larger clusters you can rotate up to 20% concurrently but only after a validation window.

Emergency rollback options
- TF state snapshot: always make a timestamped S3 copy of state before major changes. Keep at least 3 snapshots.
- AMI fallback: keep last-known-good AMI IDs in a tag format: redwood-cp:stable-YYYYMMDD. If a roll forward fails, replace instance with stable AMI and rejoin.
- Certificate rollback: restore certs from secrets-manager snapshot if new certs cause failures.
- Quick steps (if control-plane partially unhealthy):
  1) Stop new apply; scale down new nodes to prevent further quorum disruption.
  2) Reintroduce last known good node(s) from snapshot.
  3) Open incident and follow postmortem checklist.

Smoke tests & acceptance criteria (automated)
- Health endpoints respond 200 within 5s.
- API server can create and delete a namespace within 15s.
- etcd replication lag < 1s, leader stable for >30s post-change.
- No critical alerts firing for 20m after changes.

Operational play examples
- Example: rotating a control-plane node (step-by-step):
  1) Mark node for maintenance in inventory and disable autoscaler for group.
  2) kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
  3) Terraform taint aws_instance.cp-node-3 (if reprovisioning)
  4) terraform apply -target=module.cp.aws_instance.cp-node-3
  5) Wait for new node to pass healthz and metrics check, then terraform destroy old resource if not auto-terminated.
- Example: KMS key rotation (note):
  - If enable_kms_rotation=true, follow KMS rotation sequence in KMS-rotation-playbook. Ensure TF has perm to create new key versions and update secret references atomically.

Logging and observability run checks
- After apply, confirm logs are forwarded and searchable:
  - search "controlplane startup" in splunk/index=cp-logs for new boot events.
  - check metric exporter for spikes in request latency.

Loose notes / notes-to-self (rough thoughts and TODOs)
- Investigate adding explicit lifecycle.prevent_destroy on critical secrets to avoid accidental terraform destroys.
- Add a preapply script that runs DNS + connectivity checks and blocks apply if failing.
- Consider a small helper utility that will create a temporary canary cluster for testing TF plans on ephemeral infra.
- Need better mapping between TF workspace and cloud account id to reduce accidental applies to prod-like envs.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should we require image immutability guarantees (signed images) for on-prem installs? (security asked yes)
- Define exact concurrency limits for rotation based on cluster size and customer SLAs.
- Add automated smoke-test runner that reports into ticket on apply completion.

Appendix - useful commands
- terraform plan -out=tfplan.binary
- terraform apply -auto-approve tfplan.binary
- terraform state pull > state.json (for snapshotting)
- kubectl get componentstatuses && kubectl get cs
- etcdctl --endpoints=<ep> endpoint status
